subject: Seller financing: verify the note, liens, and exit terms
preheader: A comparison framework for property-specific written proposals

marketSnapshot.headline: Creative terms still require conventional due diligence
marketSnapshot.body: Seller financing can take many forms, and the legal, tax, title, licensing, disclosure, usury, servicing, lien-priority, default, and due-on-sale consequences vary. Treat every structure as a written proposal that requires review by the relevant lender, title/closing professionals, tax adviser, and local counsel.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Model the actual payment and maturity schedule
dealSpotter.body: Enter the proposed down payment, rate, amortization, maturity, balloon, fees, and payment schedule exactly as drafted. Review collateral, default, cure, transfer, prepayment, servicing, insurance, tax, and recording provisions with qualified professionals.

dealSpotter.address: Educational scenario: first lien plus seller-held junior lien
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Confirm both creditors permit the structure
dealSpotter.body: Do not assume a second lien is permitted or that an interest-only period improves the complete risk picture. Obtain written approval where required and compare total debt service, lien priority, maturity, intercreditor issues, reserves, and refinance risk.

dealSpotter.address: Educational scenario: little or no cash down
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Investigate price, condition, tenants, title, and terms
dealSpotter.body: Unusual leverage is neither proof of a bargain nor proof of a hidden defect. Verify market evidence, property condition, leases, collections, title, liens, disclosures, and the seller's authority and motivation. Decide only after the written structure and property evidence are reviewed.

blogFeature.title: Cap rate vs cash-on-cash vs DSCR — keep the capital stack visible
blogFeature.excerpt: Seller terms can change modeled cash-on-cash return and DSCR without changing the property's unlevered NOI. Compare the full written capital stack, not one output.

qa.question: When should I ask about seller financing?
qa.answer: You can ask whether a seller will consider written terms, but do not infer willingness from days on market, ownership duration, or presumed tax motives. A workable structure depends on the seller, existing debt and due-on-sale provisions, title, applicable law, tax treatment, licensing, servicing, disclosures, and your ability to perform. Have the actual proposal reviewed before relying on modeled payments or a refinance exit.
